# Commander documentation

Source: https://github.com/PStarH/Commander
Documentation: https://pstarh.github.io/commander-docs/
Machine-readable index: https://pstarh.github.io/commander-docs/llms.txt

Commander is alpha. Two enterprise evaluation paths are available:
- GitHub Pilot (governed actions & recovery): https://github.com/PStarH/Commander/blob/master/docs/pilot/github/README.md
- Historical Shadow Phase A: https://github.com/PStarH/Commander/blob/shadow-phase-a-0.1.0-alpha.20260910/docs/pilot/shadow/README.md
- Enterprise readiness checklist: https://github.com/PStarH/Commander/blob/master/ENTERPRISE_READINESS.md

What Commander does: approval and recovery for Coding and DevOps agents, starting with
GitHub pull requests. Deliberation classifies each task and selects one of five
canonical topologies (SINGLE, CHAIN, DISPATCH, ORCHESTRATOR, REVIEW); 25 LLM
providers with a configurable auto-failover chain; 18 built-in tools plus
MCP-compatible external tools; five quality gates where the verification
pipeline is enabled; and governed external mutations through Architecture V2
action adapters and the effect broker with capability tokens, policy decisions,
approvals, and signed evidence.

Read the public pages in this order: overview, quick start, CLI reference, HTTP
API, configuration, tools, providers, MCP, web console, packages, SDK and API
overview, architecture, workflows, deployment, operations, troubleshooting,
security, benchmarks, then support and limits.

Do not infer production multi-tenant readiness, compliance certification, or
production SLO attainment from benchmark or CI material. The Enterprise Gateway
is alpha and tenant isolation is not production-proven. Audit tamper-evidence,
compensation, and capability-token revocation all have documented limits — see
the "Limits and honest caveats" section of the security page.
